meta.title: Nihiltheism REN Knowledge Graph
meta.note: Expanded dataset with epistemic confidence, quotes, and topological collisions.

nodes.label: Nihiltheism
nodes.desc: A philosophical architecture in which nihilistic meaning-collapse may become a negative disclosure of an indeterminate Transcendent.
nodes.quote: Meaninglessness is treated neither as final negation nor as covert proof, but as a possible phenomenological aperture.

nodes.label: Core Thesis
nodes.desc: The collapse of objective meaning may disclose ultimacy negatively without demonstrating a determinate deity.
nodes.quote: The modality is possibility, not proof.

nodes.label: Worldly Nihilism
nodes.desc: The temporal experience of meaninglessness, alienation, finitude, dread, and the failure of ordinary projects to ground existence.

nodes.label: Transcendent Nihilism
nodes.desc: The possibility that the nihilistic encounter carries a surplus irreducible to ordinary negation and points beyond finite categories.

nodes.label: Universal Nihilistic Event
nodes.desc: A recurring phenomenological pattern: meaning-collapse, destabilized selfhood, linguistic failure, dread, and ambiguous ultimacy.

nodes.label: Meaning Collapse
nodes.desc: The breakdown of inherited, social, religious, or personal structures that previously rendered existence intelligible.

nodes.label: Groundlessness
nodes.desc: The felt and conceptual absence of a final foundation capable of justifying existence as a whole.

nodes.label: Existential Dread
nodes.desc: An affective disclosure in which beings and ordinary significance recede, exposing existence without secure ground.

nodes.label: Divided Self
nodes.desc: The oscillation between temporal involvement and a consciousness that sees through its claims to ultimacy.

nodes.label: Apophatic Unknowing
nodes.desc: A disciplined negation of predicates that refuses to convert transcendence into a positively mastered object.

nodes.label: Symbolic Rupture
nodes.desc: The moment religious and philosophical symbols confess their insufficiency and cease pretending to be literal possession of the Real.

nodes.label: Latent Divine
nodes.desc: A deliberately indeterminate name for the surplus disclosed through the failure of finite meaning and predication.

nodes.label: Recursive Negation
nodes.desc: Negation applied to its own conclusions so that neither atheistic nor theistic closure becomes dogmatic.

nodes.label: Ontic Placeholder
nodes.desc: A limit-marker occupying the position of ultimate reference without claiming determinate content.

nodes.label: Sacred Dread
nodes.desc: Dread received without therapeutic conversion into positivity, while remaining open to a transcendent register.

nodes.label: Renunciation
nodes.desc: The withdrawal of ultimacy from finite projects, desires, identities, and self-assertions.

nodes.label: Compassion after Groundlessness
nodes.desc: Compassion may arise from shared exposure to suffering and finitude, but is not logically guaranteed by the void encounter.

nodes.label: Faith–Doubt Co-Constitution
nodes.desc: Faith becomes mature not by eliminating doubt but by incorporating it as a purifying structure against idolatry.
nodes.quote: Doubt works deep within you like a disease or, even more effectively, like a faith.

nodes.label: Symbolic Insufficiency
nodes.desc: A religious symbol is most truthful when it confesses its own insufficiency.

nodes.label: Ethics without Guarantee
nodes.desc: Can ethical seriousness survive after metaphysical guarantees collapse, and on what non-arbitrary basis?

nodes.label: Martin Heidegger
nodes.desc: Anxiety, the Nothing, world-collapse, and the disclosure of beings as a whole.

nodes.label: Søren Kierkegaard
nodes.desc: Despair, faith, possibility, inwardness, and the self as a relation relating itself to itself.

nodes.label: Emil Cioran
nodes.desc: Lucid despair, futility, insomnia, doubt, and the failure of philosophical consolation.

nodes.label: Paul Tillich
nodes.desc: Nonbeing, ultimate concern, courage, symbols, and the idolatrous danger of literalism.

nodes.label: Friedrich Nietzsche
nodes.desc: The death of God, nihilism, self-overcoming, and the unresolved problem of inhabiting one’s own philosophical therapy.

nodes.label: Blaise Pascal
nodes.desc: Wretchedness, greatness, diversion, terror before infinity, and the instability of reason.

nodes.label: Thomas Ligotti
nodes.desc: Consciousness as malignancy, horror, anti-natal metaphysics, and the demolition of consolatory meaning.

nodes.label: Peter Wessel Zapffe
nodes.desc: Overdeveloped consciousness and the mechanisms by which humanity represses its existential predicament.

nodes.label: Meister Eckhart
nodes.desc: Detachment, Godhead, groundlessness, divine nothingness, and the emptying of self.

nodes.label: Nāgārjuna
nodes.desc: Emptiness, dependent arising, the emptiness of emptiness, and freedom from ontological extremes.

nodes.label: John of the Cross
nodes.desc: Dark night, purification, divine absence, and transformation through the loss of consolation.

nodes.label: Swami Vivekananda
nodes.desc: Direct realization, critique of verbal religion, Atman, and the overcoming of merely conceptual faith.

nodes.label: William James
nodes.desc: Varieties of religious experience, noetic quality, conversion, divided self, and pragmatic fruits.

nodes.label: JOURNAL314
nodes.desc: The comparative quote corpus and unified-voice evidence base spanning 53 indexed entries/voices.

nodes.label: REN Manuscript
nodes.desc: The long-form book architecture developing the abyssal, phenomenological, apophatic, and transcendent dimensions of Nihiltheism.

nodes.label: Dissertation Draft
nodes.desc: The defensible academic formulation of Nihiltheism, including scope limits, method, objections, and contribution claim.

nodes.label: Evidence Matrix
nodes.desc: Claim-to-source mapping with textual, interpretive, inferred, and speculative status labels.

nodes.label: Experiential Account
nodes.desc: First-person record of ego dissolution, timelessness, familiarity, and the return to renewed doubt.

nodes.label: Defense Dossier
nodes.desc: Committee questions, concise answers, objection trees, evidence gaps, and rehearsal notes.

defenseSimulator: What makes Nihiltheism more than a poetic redescription of apophatic theology combined with existential despair?
Why should the phenomenology of dread be treated as disclosure rather than as mood-dependent distortion?
How do you avoid converting radically different thinkers and traditions into a single “unified voice”?
Is “the Transcendent” doing explanatory work, or is it merely an ontic placeholder for what you cannot explain?
What is the strongest naturalistic account of your core experience, and why does it fail to close the question?

poleA.title: Pole A — Negative Disclosure
poleA.desc: Meaning-collapse can disclose a dimension of ultimacy inaccessible to affirmative metaphysics. Dread is not proof, but may be an epistemically distinctive mode of encounter.

poleB.title: Pole B — Psychological Projection
poleB.desc: The perceived “transcendent” surplus may be generated by cognitive destabilization, affective extremity, or retrospective interpretation rather than by an ontological disclosure.
